image_description: A close-up, eye-level shot of a vintage audio cassette tape resting on a reflective surface against a textured beige background. The cassette has a translucent amber/brown plastic casing. It features two white spools visible through circular windows, a central rectangular window showing the magnetic tape, and handwritten text in black marker on the label area. The bottom edge shows the characteristic rectangular opening for the tape head and several small circular indentations.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The object clearly exhibits the proportions of a standard compact cassette, with a wide face and thin profile consistent with the class definition.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flat rectangular prism with rounded corners.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The overall shape is a rectangle with softly rounded corners, matching the physical geometry of a cassette shell.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Two circular holes revealing tape spools inside.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Two distinct circular cutouts are present on the left and right sides, through which the internal spool mechanisms are visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Two spools of magnetic tape visible through circular holes.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: White circular structures resembling spools are clearly visible within the circular windows.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rectangular opening at bottom exposing tape for player head.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A long, narrow rectangular slot runs along the bottom edge, consistent with the mechanism exposure required for a cassette player.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface has molded details screw holes tape guide slots and write-protect tabs.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Small circular indentations (likely screw posts or mold marks) are visible along the bottom strip. A small rectangular notch (write-protect tab area) is visible on the top left corner.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The casing appears to be made of translucent amber-colored plastic, allowing some visibility of internal components, which fits the 'transparent' description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Label area on one face displaying track information artist and title.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: There is a designated label area covered in handwritten black text, simulating track/artist information.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Visible internal spools through transparent casing.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The translucency of the plastic allows the white spools to be seen, confirming the material property.

artifact_observations.location: Handwritten label on the front face
artifact_observations.reasoning: The handwritten text mimics the style of human writing but consists of nonsensical characters and pseudo-letters that do not form real words. This is a common AI artifact where the model captures the texture of writing without the semantic structure.

artifact_observations.location: Bottom edge and internal tape window
artifact_observations.reasoning: The texture of the magnetic tape in the center window appears slightly smudged or painterly rather than having the distinct sheen of mylar tape. The bottom edge details are slightly soft and lack the crisp mechanical precision of a molded plastic part.

The inner rim of the left spool window appears slightly irregular and fused with the spool itself, lacking the clean separation between the plastic shell and the internal component found in real objects.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the object is correctly identified as a cassette and not a similar rectangular object like a VHS tape or book.
To rigorously analyze the illegible/gibberish nature of the handwritten text, which is a primary artifact indicator.
To verify the structural integrity of the plastic casing, ensuring the spools are contained within the shell and edges are sharp.
To assess the realism of the lighting, reflections on the plastic, and the texture of the background surface.

focus_areas: Legibility and structure of handwritten text
Geometric precision of the rectangular slot and circular windows
Translucency and refraction effects of the plastic casing
Separation between internal spools and external casing
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the handwritten text. While it looks like writing at a glance, does it hold up to character-level scrutiny? Also, check if the 'spools' look like functional mechanical parts or just painted circles. The reflection on the table should match the curvature of the cassette bottom.
